meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and why did Owen find out from his phone?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero is based on.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. Plenty of students write somewhere else and paste it in at the end. Is that version history on your screen, or are you reading it to me from memory?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. Now, not later.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is careless, not proof of anything. And I still haven't seen your screen, Hale.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft; that's what an outline is for. Three claims and you haven't put a single page in front of me.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.

Your own note of a conversation is your impression, written by the person who wanted to give the zero. Owen gets cornered by a teacher and freezes; that tells me nothing about who wrote his essay. Was anyone else in the room?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend with a spell-checker, of course they look different. You've been building a file on my son since September, Hale, so tell me where this ends.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then leave it out of the room; I've got the vendor's own guide in my bag saying it can't stand alone. You still haven't answered me: what happens to his mark?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4, and I'll take it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, not in front of his class, marked in time for his December 1 applications, and nothing on his file, all in writing tonight. The rest of my questions go in my email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Okay. And it's marked before December 1, or none of this works.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
I'll confirm a day with him and put it in my email tonight. Your letter says this week, in those words.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Marked this week, before December 1. Otherwise, yes.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Copies of every document you described today, attached to that letter. And tell me who else has seen this.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, not in front of his class, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still want copies of every document you described, the names of everyone who has seen this, and the rewrite marked this week, before December 1. I expect your letter tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero with nothing on his record; she still wants copies of your documents, to know who else has seen this, and the rewrite marked this week before December 1, and that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You put procedure 4.4 on the table only after owning the zero and laying out several dated pieces of evidence, which met her one demand that could never bend, his record.
What cost ground: Nothing pushed her back, but you described each document without ever turning the screen, so she kept attacking each piece and none of them stood on its own.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history from 11:31 to 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, came very close to that kind of night, which is why she wrote the times down and went straight to defending him. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she told you to pull up the version history, turn the screen right then and answer her point about pasting from somewhere else before you move on to the quotation.
